name: Imprinting Disorders

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Imprinting Disorders

criteria.description: Detection of abnormal methylation patterns at imprinted loci by molecular testing
Presence of characteristic clinical features consistent with known imprinting syndromes (e.g., growth abnormalities, developmental delay)
Family history suggestive of imprinting disorder or related epigenetic abnormalities
Identification of uniparental disomy or copy number variations affecting imprinted regions

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Molecular confirmation of imprinting defect plus presence of characteristic clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires integration of molecular, clinical, and family history data.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Growth restriction or overgrowth with imprinting pattern
pathognomonic.notes: Includes intrauterine growth retardation or macrosomia depending on disorder subtype
searchTerms: too small or large growth with genetic imprinting
growth delays or excess linked to imprinting

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distinctive craniofacial dysmorphism characteristic of specific imprinting syndromes
pathognomonic.notes: Examples include triangular face in Silver-Russell syndrome or round face in Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome
searchTerms: distinctive facial features from imprinting disorders
unique head and face shape abnormalities

pathognomonic.symptomName: Epigenetic methylation abnormalities at imprinted loci

common.notes: Variable severity depending on specific disorder
Often due to poor suck or gastrointestinal dysmotility

occasional.notes: May be present depending on syndrome subtype
Mild and transient in some cases

occasional.symptomName: Behavioral abnormalities including autism spectrum features

rare.symptomName: Wilms tumor or other embryonal tumors

laboratory: Abnormal methylation patterns at imprinted loci detected by methylation-specific PCR or array
Hypoglycemia with hyperinsulinemia in neonatal period
Elevated IGF2 levels in some overgrowth syndromes
imaging: Ultrasound detection of organomegaly or tumor masses (e.g., Wilms tumor)
MRI brain showing structural abnormalities in some cases
genetic: Copy number variations affecting imprinted regions
Point mutations in imprinting control regions
other: Characteristic dysmorphic features on clinical examination
Family history of imprinting disorders or related epigenetic abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Predominant growth restriction with specific methylation defects
Absence of overgrowth features seen in Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome
Hypotonia and hyperphagia leading to obesity
Loss of paternal gene expression on chromosome 15q11-q13

redFlags: Severe intrauterine growth restriction or macrosomia with dysmorphic features
Neonatal hypoglycemia refractory to standard treatment
Family history of imprinting disorders or unexplained developmental delay
references: Eggermann T, et al. Imprinting disorders: a group of congenital disorders with overlapping patterns of molecular changes affecting imprinted loci. Clin Epigenetics. 2015.
Buiting K. Prader-Willi syndrome and Angelman syndrome. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2010.
Weksberg R, et al. Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome. Eur J Hum Genet. 2010.
